question: what constant must be added to gen1 at Elba to place it on surveyed NAVD88(GEOID18), and do independent control points agree?

gen1 2008 MN DNR tile: the corridor the swath chain is solved in
gen1 2008 MN DNR tile holding a checkpoint (outside the corridor row; its along-track offset is reported)
elbaext datum + per-swath alignment; swath 133 is the reference frame the tie is expressed in
surveyed 3DEP QA checkpoints near Elba, NAVD88(GEOID18)

params.name: checkpoint_set
params.why: the six 3DEP vertical-accuracy marks within ~12 km of Elba, transcribed in ABSOLUTE_ELEVATION_REFS.md section 1a

params.name: verdict_tolerance_mm
params.why: gen1 per-county vertical RMSEz for Winona, InPort 68818, ABSOLUTE_ELEVATION_REFS.md section 1b

params.name: covering_line_radius_m
params.why: ELBAEXT2_SCOPE.md section 2 counts covering returns within 10 m of each mark (173-201 class-2 returns there); it only decides which lines are candidate chain sources, not which returns enter the tie

params.name: csf_crop_halfwidth_m
params.why: CSF is run on a crop, not a tile, to keep it seconds instead of minutes; 300 m gives a 600 m box (~350k gen1 points) so the cloth is not dominated by the crop edge. It excludes nothing from the estimate: the widest fitting radius is 25 m.

params.name: target_lines
params.why: the gen1 swaths of the elbaext product; swath 133 is its reference (0,0,0)

params.name: elbaext_lateral_shift_m
params.why: corrections_geoid.json cross_epoch_datum horizontal_shift_m -- the Nuth-Kaaab shift that puts gen1 in gen2's (and the checkpoints') horizontal frame; reported both applied and not

params.name: link_exclude_classes
params.why: coreg.coregister_swaths terrain proxy ~isin(classification,(5,6,9)) -- the VENDOR classification, so no CSF is needed for the chain

columns.R_m: radius of the fitting window about the checkpoint, m
columns.n: ground returns inside the report radius, count
columns.tie_mm: constant to ADD to gen1 in swath-133 frame to reach the surveyed datum, mm
columns.fit_rms_mm: RMS of z_i - S(x_i,y_i) for the local surface fit S, mm
columns.medres_mm: median of those residuals -- the slope-normal quantile term, mm
columns.relief_m: p95 - p05 of return elevations inside the radius, m
columns.n_lines: distinct flight lines contributing returns inside the radius, count
columns.scan_deg: |scan angle| p05/p50/p95 of those returns, degrees (0 = nadir)
columns.area_km2: measured overlap area of the pair on the solve grid, km^2
columns.cells: grid cells used in the Nuth & Kaeaeb fit, count
columns.dz_mm: vertical shift to add to src to align it onto ref, mm
columns.nmad0_mm: robust scatter of the overlap difference before the link, mm
columns.nmad1_mm: and after -- the residual the link could not remove, mm
columns.dx_m: eastward shift to add to src, m
columns.dy_m: northward shift to add to src, m
columns.type: NVA = open ground, VVA = under vegetation (3DEP convention)
columns.line: gen1 flight line (point_source_id) covering the mark
columns.links: cross-swath links between that line and the elbaext frame, count
columns.sigma_mm: half the tie's spread across the pipeline-scale radii, mm
columns.tie_med_mm: the tie taken as the median over the pipeline-scale radii, mm
columns.chain_mm: chain-accumulated vertical shift into the elbaext frame, mm
columns.chain_sig: per-link sigmas of that shift in quadrature, mm
columns.geoid_mm: references.geoid_difference GEOID03->GEOID18 at the mark, mm
columns.usable: does the radius spread fall inside the verdict tolerance
columns.pair: which two results are being compared
columns.what: what a disagreement between them would mean
columns.dN_km: northing offset of the mark from the corridor band centre, km
columns.swath: gen1 flight line whose fitted along-track drift curve is summarised
columns.p2p_mm: peak-to-peak of that fitted drift curve, mm
columns.span_km: along-track distance the curve covers, km (gps_time x 76 m/s)
columns.mm_per_km: peak-to-peak divided by span -- the scale of the drift term this module does NOT correct, mm/km
columns.note: why a checkpoint has no tie, where it has none
